speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; can you tell me when these symptoms started and if they came on suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; given your history of steroid use and diabetes, have you noticed any muscle wasting in the right arm or any numbness spreading to your hand? Also, do you experience any neck pain or radiating pain down your arm?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Paraneoplastic Sensory Neuronopathy (likely secondary to an underlying malignancy given the weight loss, age, and steroid use).

REQUEST TEST: CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis, Serum Protein Electrophoresis, and Tumor Markers.
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Cervical Spine.
